AGENTS.md — Developer and AI Agent Guidelines for paramix

Source: AGENTS.md

This guide explains the architecture, coding conventions, testing standards, and development workflow for contributors and AI coding agents working on paramix.

1. Role, Scope & Package Architecture

paramix (Aggregate and Disaggregate Continuous Parameters for Compartmental Models) is an R package within the ACCIDDA organization providing a convenient framework for aggregating continuously varying parameters for compartmental models and subsequent upscaling (distillation) of model outcomes to high resolution.

  • Package Scope:
    • Continuous Parameter Translation: Discretizing continuous or high-resolution parameters (f_param, e.g., age-varying infection fatality ratio or case fatality ratio) across population density distributions (f_pop, e.g., demographic pyramids) onto lower-resolution compartmental model partitions.
    • Alembic Engine (alembic): Constructing the core mixing table as the union of model and output partitions, calculating exact integration weights (∫cici+1f(x)ρ(x)dx\int_{c_i}^{c_{i+1}} f(x)\rho(x)\,\mathrm{d}x) and relative populations (∫cici+1ρ(x)dx\int_{c_i}^{c_{i+1}} \rho(x)\,\mathrm{d}x).
    • Parameter Blending (blend): Extracting population-weighted aggregate parameters for model partitions (∑weight/∑relpop\sum \text{weight} / \sum \text{relpop}).
    • Outcome Distillation (distill): Upscaling coarse model outcomes (e.g., compartment deaths or infections) into high-resolution output partitions using Bayesian proportional allocation (weighti/∑weightj\text{weight}_i / \sum \text{weight}_j).
    • Comparison & Summary Utilities (parameter_summary, distill_summary): Diagnostic summaries and tabular comparisons across continuous, midpoint, naive, and integrated aggregation schemes.

2. Core Tenets & Development Workflows

The justfile as Single Source of Truth

  • All builds, linting, formatting, tests, documentation generation, and site previews must be performed via justfile recipes.
  • CI workflows (.github/workflows/*.yaml) invoke just <recipe>.

Common recipes:

just format        # Format R code using air
just lint          # Check formatting and linting (air + lintr)
just docs          # Regenerate man/*.Rd, NAMESPACE, R/globals.R
just install       # Install development version of package
just test          # Run testthat test suite
just test-fast     # Run test suite stopping on first failure
just coverage      # Check test coverage via covr
just spell         # Check documentation spelling
just site          # Fast build of pkgdown documentation site
just site-full     # Full build of pkgdown documentation site with install
just check         # Build and check package tarball
just check-cran    # Check package with --as-cran

3. R Coding & Quality Standards

Code Formatting (air) & Linting (lintr)

  • All R files must adhere to air formatting (indent-width = 2, line-width = 80).
  • lintr enforces line length ≤100\le 100, snake_case naming (allowing paramix, ERR_, MSG_), and implicit returns.
  • Always run just format && just lint before finishing any task.

Error Messages & Signaling Standards

  • Define centralized error and warning format strings at the top of R files:

    ERR_INPUT_FILE_MISSING <- "input file '{filename}' was not found in directory '{dir}'"

  • Use named {var} placeholders rather than unnamed format tokens.

  • Format code entities (function names, formal parameters, R expressions) with backticks (`code`).

  • Format user-supplied values, paths, and column names with single quotes ('value').

Documentation (roxygen2)

  • Use Markdown-formatted roxygen comments.
  • Always use explicit @title and @description tags in roxygen blocks.
  • Unexported internal functions should be marked with @keywords internal and @noRd to keep code documented in source without generating unused .Rd files.
  • Document @param concisely with type and default where applicable.
  • Document @return explicitly describing return type and structure.
  • For exported functions, include runnable and fast @examples (or @examplesIf require(...)).

Documentation and Vignette Voice

  • Write user-facing prose in active voice with a clear actor.
  • Prefer direct phrasing such as “We designed paramix to aggregate continuous parameters” or “This workflow allocates compartment outcomes to individual years of age” rather than passive phrasing such as “paramix is designed to be used for…” or “parameters are often aggregated by…”.
  • Where possible, avoid pronouns in explanatory prose. Use a noun instead: for example, “the function calculates” instead of “it calculates”. However, “we” for authorial voice and “you” for the reader are preferred.
  • Keep the subject explicit and the action concrete. Explain the problem, what the package does, and why it matters in plain English before you expand into implementation details.
  • Use a conversational but formal tone. Favor strong verbs and concrete nouns over heavy jargon, abstract nominalizations, and repeated to be constructions.
  • Define domain terms once and use them consistently across roxygen comments, vignettes, and package docs.

Unit Testing (testthat)

  • All user-facing functions must have comprehensive test coverage in tests/testthat/.
  • Test both expected success paths and error conditions.
  • Assert on error messages using exact regex or template pattern matching.
  • Ensure tests run cleanly across Linux, macOS, and Windows.

4. Git & Commit Guidelines

  • Maintain a clean git history.
  • Keep commit messages descriptive and focused.
  • Do not commit generated build artifacts (*.tar.gz, *.Rcheck/, docs/, man/*.Rd, R/globals.R).
